summary: The Himalayas are the tallest mountain range on Earth, formed by colliding tectonic plates and home to Mount Everest.
introduce: Read the title “The Himalayas: Roof of the World” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: the height of something above sea level
one of the huge pieces of rock that make up the Earth's outer layer and slowly move
to crash into something with great force

challengeTerms.def: relating to the huge moving plates that make up the Earth's crust
the height of a place above sea level
a long, carefully organized journey made for a specific and often difficult purpose

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that mountains that are still growing are more interesting than mountains that stay the same? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the Himalayas formed and why melting glaciers matter for people far from the mountains.
struggling: Pre-teach altitude, plate, and collide with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses tectonic, elevation, and expedition to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
